answer: The registry issues a random graph per applicant; registration requires a zero-knowledge proof of a Hamiltonian cycle through it, with the cycle itself hidden. Finding the cycle sends a ripple through the graph: the search is the real work, the proof leaks nothing. A copper thread of the cycle is committed without revealing it, and a forge of fresh randomness mints each graph per key, so bulk Sybil creation scales linearly with hard search work.
